articles.title: ‘Philippines to buy 100% of farm products, energy from US’
articles.summary: The Philippines has agreed to buy all its agricultural and energy requirements from the US, President Donald Trump said days after his bilateral meeting with President Marcos, who had emphasized the…

blocks.text: November 22, 2026 | 12:00am
Trump invokes Philippines -US security relations

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines has agreed to buy all its agricultural and energy requirements from the US, President Donald Trump said days after his bilateral meeting with President Marcos, who had emphasized the need for the country to have diverse sources of supply of commodities.
Trump said the Philippines was buying a lot of its farm products from other countries, including Brazil, prompting him to ask Marcos to source all its agricultural needs from the US.

“And the Philippines, as you know, was buying a lot of their farm product from other countries, including Brazil, much more than from us. And I said, here’s the deal, you buy 100 percent of your agriculture from January 1st from our farmers,” he told reporters at the White House yesterday (Philippine time).

“We’re the greatest farmers in the world with the greatest equipment in the world. You know, we support these countries, but they don’t buy from us. So I said, you are going to buy 100 percent of your farm product, not 90, not 95,” he added.
At a media interview in China on Friday, Marcos admitted the two countries would like to finalize a trade deal, but there was no mention of buying all of the Philippines’ requirements from the US.
According to Trump, the Philippines would be buying “billions and billions of dollars” of farm products from the US.

“Is Brazil going to help them in case they get into a little skirmish with China? I don’t think so. They buy from Brazil and other countries, and now they’re buying from us 100 percent, not 99 percent,” the US president said.

“They buy it mostly from the Middle East. Can you believe it?” he added. “I said, ‘If China attacks you, is the Middle East going to come to your rescue?’ ‘No, sir.’ ‘Well, that’s good. Don’t buy from them anymore.”

Marcos and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva held a bilateral meeting in the Philippines last Nov. 14 to discuss ways to boost partnership in renewable energy and biofuels, livestock production and animal health, modern farming, education, science and technology, law enforcement and other fields.
Trump claimed the Philippines would also purchase 100 percent of its energy requirements from the US.

“Also, energy, they buy 20 percent from us, but they buy – I said, where do you get your energy? I was with Prime Minister Marcos, who’s a very good man, by the way. Great family. But I said, where do you buy your energy? Should we buy it from the Middle East? I said, not anymore, you don’t,” he said, erroneously referring to the President as prime minister.
“You’re going to buy 100 percent of your energy from us, yes, sir. So instead of having a deficit, we have a huge – I could do this with every country.”
Diversified sources
In China last Friday, Marcos said the Philippines needs to diversify its sources of key commodities, emphasizing that nothing was discussed about buying all of Manila’s requirements from Washington.

“The trade deal is a response to the tariff schedule that the US tried to impose. They imposed it but it was struck down in court. But anyway, it still brought open the question of the trade between the US and the Philippines,” Marcos said.
“And it is timely because the Philippines, as you know, is looking for many, many, many ways to expand, to diversify our sources of supply of different commodities,” he added.
Marcos said the conflict between Russia and Ukraine highlighted the need for the Philippines to find new trade partners.

“We are continuing to open new partners to engage, new engagements, to have new engagements, to have new partnerships with everybody around the world. So that the way I put it is that if you’re standing on one foot, if you rely on just one party, it would be prone to problems. If you rely on several parties, even if one of them encounters problems, you can run to the others,” the President said.
“And that’s why the trade deal is important. And we are proposing to buy more agricultural products for one thing,” he added.
The negotiations, Marcos said, covered more purchases of farm products from the US, including soybeans and wheat.
“We are looking for cheaper sources of food products. We are looking for cheaper sources for energy importation. And that is – the bulk of our discussion with President Trump was that,” he said.

“So there is the trade deal, which is the result of the tariff schedule that the US attempted to impose, but nonetheless opened the discussion on trade. And there was the specific on energy and agricultural products during the meeting with President Trump.”
A White House statement said Trump has also announced the Philippines’ commitment to “eliminate the US trade deficit with the Philippines.” — Louella Desidero

articles.title: Duterte camp to ICC: Exclude recorded testimony of ex-DDS
articles.summary: The defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte has urged the trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) to exclude the recorded testimony of a former police officer who claimed to…

blocks.text: Headlines
November 22, 2026 | 12:00am
Photos courtesy of the International Criminal Court show former president Rodrigo Duterte during his first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025.
Photos / ICC | via Janvic Mateo

MANILA, Philippines — The defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte has urged the trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) to exclude the recorded testimony of a former police officer who claimed to be a former member of the so-called Davao death squad (DDS).
In a 12-page filing dated Nov. 18, defense lawyer Peter Haynes opposed the prosecution’s request to admit the prior recorded testimony of the witness identified as “P-0002.”
The prosecution, in its original request, described the witness as a former Davao City Police officer who was part of the death squad.

“P-0002’s evidence supports the existence of a policy to neutralize alleged criminals in Davao City, as shown by, (i) the provision of financial incentives; (ii) the use of State and civilian forces and (iii) the dissemination of this policy by Mr. Duterte to the perpetrators,” read the Nov. 5 filing of acting prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang.

Niang requested the Trial Chamber III to allow the recorded testimony of the witness as he is no longer available to testify during the trial. It was unclear why the witness is no longer available to testify.
According to Haynes, admitting P-0002’s recorded testimony would be prejudicial to Duterte as the defense would not be able to cross examine him during trial proceedings.
“P-0002’s statement contains repeated references to Mr. Duterte’s acts and conduct, on which the prosecution places heavy reliance in its trial brief,” the defense lawyer said.
These include allegations on Duterte’s supposed role in establishing the death squad, as well as direct orders to commit various crimes.
Haynes also questioned the probative value of the recorded testimony, claiming that P-0002 is an unreliable witness.
ICC case strong
Former United Nations special rapporteur on extrajudicial executions Agnès Callamard is confident the ICC will convict Duterte for crimes against humanity.
Callamard, now secretary general of Amnesty International, told The STAR on Friday there is enough evidence to establish Duterte’s role in the alleged crimes.

“Sadly for ex-president Duterte, he has left behind much evidence of his commitment to killings. He has made many public statements. He has called for others to kill. He has demanded killings. He has done so over and over and over again,” he said.

“It’s not about the number of cases. It is about demonstrating the organized nature of the killings, and I suspect that the International Criminal Court has all the evidence that it needs,” she added.
Despite the ongoing proceedings at The Hague, Callamard maintained the Philippine government still has a lot to do to ensure that all victims attain justice.
“Handing over Duterte to the International Criminal Court was a good thing, but it is not enough. They now need to take a step to tackle the culture of impunity within the Philippines,” she said.

articles.title: Gatchalian lauds JV for weeding out P97 billion ‘non-compliant’ projects
articles.summary: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian lauded finance committee chairman Sen. JV Ejercito for being stricter than him in handling the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, which saw P97.5…

blocks.text: November 22, 2026 | 12:00am
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian and Senator JV Ejercito
The Philippine STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian lauded finance committee chairman Sen. JV Ejercito for being stricter than him in handling the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, which saw P97.5 billion in public works projects excised for being non-compliant.
Speaking to radio dzMM yesterday, Gatchalian said he also removed questionable budget items when he was finance committee chair that scrutinized the 2026 national budget.

While technical descriptions were required last year, the finance committee now under Ejercito is requiring more documentation, like programs of works, certificates of implementability, Regional Development Council approval and correct geotagging coordinates.
Gatchalian said his own research flagged 295 public works projects worth P8.836 billion based on the executive’s spending plan, the National Expenditure Program.
He was shocked that the current finance committee weeded out up to P97.5 billion in noncompliant projects under the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)’s proposed outlay.
“From P8.8 billion to P90-plus billion. I was surprised how strict Senator JV is. When he gives a deadline, finished or not finished, pass your paper,” Gatchalian said.
“And that’s correct. What we started in 2026 has become stricter,” he added.
Gatchalian welcomed the Senate move to reverse the cuts in foreign-assisted projects (FAPs) done by the House of Representatives in the latter’s version of the General Appropriations Bill (GAB).
Among the projects with restored government counterpart funding are the Metro Manila Subway, North-South Commuter Railway, Cavite-Bataan bridge and the Laguna Lakeshore road network.
“There’s a big difference between the Senate committee report and House GAB. The foreign-assisted projects were restored. The Senate rule now is no supporting documents, no budget,” Gatchalian said.
He said the finance committee under Ejercito will sponsor the budget tomorrow, signaling the start of marathon plenary debates on different agencies’ proposed budgets.

Gatchalian vowed that the Senate would finish its plenary debates in record time to pass the budget on final reading and immediately hold a bicameral conference committee meeting with the House to reconcile their conflicting GAB versions, to meet its target of ratifying the budget before Dec. 17 or the session adjournment.

articles.title: PPP plans for 9 airports, railway projects bared
articles.summary: Nine regional airports across the country are being readied for development under public-private partnership arrangement by next year, Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon announced on Friday.

blocks.text: November 22, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Nine regional airports across the country are being readied for development under public-private partnership (PPP) arrangement by next year, Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon announced on Friday.
The airports eyed for PPP are in Davao, Siargao, Bicol, Iloilo, Bacolod, Puerto Princesa, Busuanga, General Santos and Tacloban.

Speaking at the Stratbase Institute’s Pilipinas Conference 2026, Dizon said the Department of Transportation (DOTr) would begin with a bundled PPP covering the airports in Davao, Siargao and Bicol, which is expected to be awarded in the first quarter of 2027. The proposal, submitted by the group operating the Clark International Airport, is an unsolicited offer covering the development and operation of the three airports.

Dizon, who assumed his post after a Cabinet reshuffle earlier this month, said these projects were part of the administration’s broader push to finish infrastructure projects that had been stalled for years.

“(When he started), the President said that PPPs are the most important legacy that the President, this administration, is going to leave behind. And today, for airports, we have already privatized the most PPPs that any other administration has... nine airports will be PPPed by the time the President exits in June of 2028,” he said.
“That will really change the way our airports are run,” he added.
The DOTr, he added, will also pursue solicited PPPs for the Iloilo airport in the first half of 2027, followed by Bacolod, Puerto Princesa, Busuanga, General Santos and Tacloban airports.
Dizon said the administration had already pursued the PPP model for three airports, including the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA), as well as the Bohol and Bicol airports.
Aside from airports, the DOTr is also preparing PPP arrangement for three major Metro Manila railway systems.

These include the Light Rail Transit Line 2 (LRT-2) and the Metro Rail Transit Line 3 (MRT-3). The department is also planning a PPP for the automated fare collection system covering the country’s major railway networks, including the Metro Manila Subway and the North-South Commuter Railway.

The solicited PPP for LRT-2, with assistance from the International Finance Corp. of the World Bank, and the MRT-3 project, with support from the Asian Development Bank, are targeted for completion next year.
Dizon also announced the opening before Christmas of the Cavite-Laguna Expressway (CALAX), which is 97 percent complete.
The first phase of the Toll Road 4 (TR4), connecting Laguna to Lucena, is expected to open early next year.
Stratbase Institute president Dindo Manhit said the investments are important, especially after the Philippines concluded its 2026 chairship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

“The true measure of our ASEAN leadership will not simply be the meetings convened, declarations adopted or initiatives launched. It will be the partnerships we sustain, the opportunities we create and the regional priorities we continue to champion long after our chairship has ended,” Manhit said in his speech.
He stressed that economic initiatives must respond to the everyday concerns of Filipino households, including affordable necessities, employment and reliable public services.
“Filipinos want an economy that works for them. They want affordable necessities, decent jobs, reliable public services and opportunities to improve their lives,” he said.

Manhit said strategic partnerships, including initiatives such as the Luzon Economic Corridor involving the Philippines, the United States and Japan, must translate into investments, stronger industries and better-paying jobs.
“Our strategic partnerships must deliver results that Filipinos can feel – not just opportunities that look good on paper,” he said.

articles.title: Senate impeach court set to take short break
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court will go on a brief hiatus this week, with trial sessions set to resume on Dec. 1, as the tribunal targets a final judgment before Congress adjourns on Dec. 18.

blocks.text: November 22, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court will go on a brief hiatus this week, with trial sessions set to resume on Dec. 1, as the tribunal targets a final judgment before Congress adjourns on Dec. 18.

Under the updated schedule, the court canceled its Nov. 26-27 hearings after lead defense counsel Sheila Sison manifested that the remaining eight to 10 defense witnesses are unavailable due to prior commitments.

Impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol said exhibit marking and the submission of the defense’s sequential witness list will still proceed during the week, while the Senate will hold plenary voting on the national budget on Nov. 28.
Hearings from Dec. 1 to 4 are earmarked to wrap up the defense’s presentation of evidence, followed by the formal offer of evidence from Dec. 9 to 11.
“Barring rebuttal or sur-rebuttal extensions,” the court aims to hold oral arguments and its final roll-call vote on Dec. 14 and Dec. 16 to 18.
Enough time
The targeted remaining three weeks in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte would be enough time for her defense team to present its last five to six witnesses.
Defense spokesman Michael Poa said the given time frame would be enough for Duterte’s legal team to complete its presentation of evidence.
“We were already able to take up three (witnesses) this week and then we dispensed with one. So, we’re down to around five or six,” Poa said.

“Of course, I would be a little biased by saying, yes, (the testimony of the remaining witness) will be impactful. So, definitely in our minds, in our perspective, it will be impactful because we want to end strong,” he added.
Tight schedule

Speaking to dzMM and dwIZ yesterday, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said he is looking at a very “tight” schedule in December for the ongoing impeachment proceedings, with the defense set to present their last witness and make their formal offer of evidence, and for the prosecution to respond or rebut.

Asked if there are enough days in December for the formal offer and their verdict writing break, Gatchalian said some senator-judges, like himself, have started making their analysis of the evidence presented so far to save on time.

“Of course, it’s not over yet. More evidence is still coming in. We have also begun discussing amongst ourselves. What’s important is the explanation of votes – to clarify to the public the reasons behind our vote,” he said.

Gatchalian said it was still his “personal” preference for the whole trial to end with a verdict before Christmas or New Year’s. But he admitted that the court has to be “flexible” as it cannot predict what will happen in December, with the defense set to present their last set of witnesses from Dec. 1 to 4.
He said one of the lessons of the impeachment court is to be flexible.
“We have an idea in terms of the number of days, but we remain flexible to ensure the trial runs efficiently,” Gatchalian said.

He said the before Christmas verdict date is a “moving target” similar to the Senate’s target date for passing and ratifying the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, and in confirming the Cabinet secretaries, foreign service and military officers whose appointments and nominations have to be confirmed before Dec. 17 or the session adjournment lest they be bypassed.
Twelve Cabinet secretaries are in line for confirmation before the Commission on Appointments (CA) after having served in acting capacity for over a year.

Gatchalian said their legislative duties in the budget and CA are equally important, with the budget being “time-bound” that requires being passed before year-end, and the confirmation process is needed to end the practice of having officials in an acting capacity.
He said all these “important activities” – impeachment, budget plenary deliberations and confirmation process – “are being done by the Senate simultaneously.” — Bella Cariaso, Marc Jayson Cayabyab

articles.title: Tree-planting drive and Cale88: No link, says OVP
articles.summary: The Office of the Vice President maintained that its nationwide tree-planting program has no connection with Cale88 Foods Corp. after it was raised by the House prosecution team during the…

blocks.text: November 22, 2026 | 12:00am

“The Office of the Vice President categorically denies any association between its ‘Pagbabago: A Million Trees Campaign’ and Cale88 Foods Corporation’s compliance with the Board of Investments (BOI) tree-planting requirement,” the OVP said in a statement.
Inday Sara Duterte?

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Vice President (OVP) maintained that its nationwide tree-planting program has no connection with Cale88 Foods Corp. after it was raised by the House prosecution team during the impeachment trial against VP Sara Duterte on Friday.

Prosecution counsel Erwin Matib asked defense witness Trade Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo Rodolfo if Duterte’s tree-planting program was connected to a BOI requirement for enterprises to plant at least 100 forest trees to qualify for incentives.

“Any attempt to link the Vice President’s participation in the OVP’s environmental initiatives to Cale88 Foods Corporation’s BOI compliance is misleading, malicious and has no factual basis,” the OVP added.

Rodolfo said Cale88 Foods Corp., the banana chips exporter co-owned by Duterte’s husband Manases Carpio and her dentist Lourdes Lebosada, takes its name from the first two letters of their surnames paired with a number symbolizing infinity.

“The ‘Pagbabago: A Million Trees Campaign” is an independent environmental initiative of the OVP, launched on March 27, 2023 in support of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources’ efforts to reduce carbon emissions and address climate change. The program is part of the OVP’s advocacy to protect the environment for future generations,” the OVP added.
It said the campaign, in partnership with various government agencies and private sectors, has planted 1,386,682 trees nationwide.

“Amid these allegations and political insinuations, the OVP remains steadfast in fulfilling its mandate of delivering efficient, accessible and responsive public service for the good of all Filipinos,” the OVP said.

The firm has drawn scrutiny during Duterte’s impeachment trial after Sen. Risa Hontiveros flagged its foreign remittances – including funds from Chinese entities and a Ukrainian company facing criminal complaints for money laundering and fraud.

Financial forensic expert Alexander Cabrera previously testified that Cale88’s financial statements lacked reported accounts receivable, accounts payable and raw material inventory, despite substantial cash inflows and outflows.

The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) earlier reported that the firm grossed more than P1 billion at one point and received P776 million in foreign remittances from 2022 to 2025, including P319 million from China.
Onion-skinned?
Duterte should not be onion-skinned regarding the reported link between her tree-planting activities and Calle88 Foods Corp., according to the spokesman of the House prosecution panel.

Lanao del Sur 1st District. Rep. Zia Alontio Adiong said at the Saturday News Forum in Quezon City Duterte seemed to be very sensitive when House prosecutors raised questions on whether photographs of a tree-planting activity which she attended had something to do with the BOI’s tree-planting requirement.
Adiong reminded Duterte that probing questions are part of cross-examinations during regular court trials.
Adiong said prosecutors believe Cale88 is a shell company which earned profits with only two employees, aside from an alleged P319-million financial inflow from China.
The lawmaker said there is nothing wrong if the tree-planting activity is part of Cale88’s compliance requirement with the BOI. — Emmanuel Tupas

articles.title: Bullies face expulsion under new rules, says DepEd chief
articles.summary: Students found guilty of bullying may face expulsion under a new Department of Education policy, Education Secretary Sonny Angara warned yesterday amid a reported incident involving students in Aklan.

blocks.text: November 22, 2026 | 12:00am
Children play at the schoolyard of Diosdado Macapagal Elementary school in Quezon City in this file photo from January of this year.
Michael Varcas

MANILA, Philippines — Students found guilty of bullying may face expulsion under a new Department of Education policy, Education Secretary Sonny Angara warned yesterday amid a reported incident involving students in Aklan.

“We strongly condemn all forms of bullying in our schools. Every child deserves to learn in a safe environment, free from fear, harassment and violence. As the author of the Anti-Bullying Act of 2013 when I was a legislator, protecting children has been part of my advocacy. At DepEd, we have further strengthened this protection by updating the law’s implementing rules,” Angara said on Facebook.
Angara was referring to an alleged bullying incident involving students of Ciriaco L. Icamina Sr. National High School in Malinao, Aklan.
“Under DepEd Order 006, s. 2026, or the ESMLE Policy, we are further intensifying our response to bullying, including expulsion as a possible disciplinary sanction,” he added.

Angara urged the public to refrain from speculation and sharing unverified information, particularly photos and videos of the children involved, as the DepEd’s Aklan division investigates the incident.
“Let us not add to the trauma or put the children involved in the incident in a more difficult situation,” he said.
The secretary also vowed to hold accountable anyone found to have violated the law.
“We will continue to ensure that every school is a safe place where children can learn without fear. This is our commitment to every parent and every child in the country,” he said.

articles.title: COP31 climate summit risks failure as talks go deep into overtime
articles.summary: Negotiators expected a revised draft on November 20. But by the afternoon of November 21, with no new text on the table, hopes for significant changes have faded and frustration is mounting.

blocks.text: EMPTY. Cameras are set up as talks stretch into overtime at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, on November 21, 2026.
Murad Sezer/Reuters
Negotiators expected a revised draft on November 20. But by the afternoon of November 21, with no new text on the table, hopes for significant changes have faded and frustration is mounting.

items: The COP31 climate summit is facing significant challenges, with negotiators from nearly 200 countries struggling to reach an agreement on fossil fuels and climate finance, leading to delays in the talks.

EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra emphasized that the outcome will either be a good deal or no deal, while Turkey's COP31 President Murat Kurum called for responsible actions from all countries to avoid jeopardizing the process.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

ANTALYA, Turkey – The COP31 climate summit will either produce a good deal or no deal at all, the European Union’s top climate official said on Saturday, November 21, as talks stretched deep into overtime.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance, delaying an agreement at the two-week conference that had been scheduled to end on Friday, November 20.
“It’s either going to be a good deal, or it’s going to be no deal,” EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra told reporters.
Asked about the chances of no deal emerging, he said, “We will find out.”
The last major breakdown in UN climate talks came in Copenhagen in 2009, when countries failed to adopt the Copenhagen Accord by consensus in a setback for multilateral climate diplomacy.

As workers dismantled catering stands and exhibits at the venue, delegations shuttled between meeting rooms to discuss tactics, while others rested as they awaited a new version of the negotiating text.
Turkey’s COP31 President Murat Kurum met officials from the EU, Australia and Saudi Arabia in an effort to break the deadlock, but acknowledged a deal could prove elusive.
“I call on every country to act responsibly,” he told reporters. “There is no benefit for anyone to ruin this process by getting hung up on words, phrases.”
The biggest sticking points are whether a final agreement should mention the fossil fuels driving global warming and whether it should include support for poorer countries adapting to climate change.
A draft deal published on Thursday, November 19, removed earlier references to ending fossil fuel use. Observers said Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers had opposed the language.
The draft also dropped a proposed $120 billion target for finance to help developing countries adapt to climate change.
Negotiators had expected a revised draft on Friday. But by Saturday afternoon, with no new text on the table, hopes for significant changes had faded and frustration was mounting.
Recent climate summits have regularly overrun without collapsing, eventually producing agreements.
Isatou Camara, Gambia’s finance negotiator, said some countries appeared to be using delay tactics to pressure others into accepting a weaker outcome.
“This delay strategy, which has been used at previous COPs, could be so at the end when things are put on the table you accept because you are fed up, exhausted, and want to go home,” she said.
This year’s talks have been further complicated by war and rising living costs, which are competing for the attention of policymakers and the public.

The US, the world’s largest historical greenhouse gas emitter, is also absent from the talks for the second year in a row after President Donald Trump ended cooperation on climate policy, calling global warming a hoax.

A UN report last month found the world is on track to exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) of warming above pre-industrial levels, a threshold governments agreed under the 2015 Paris Agreement to try to avoid breaching.
The draft agreement acknowledges that projected overshoot and calls for faster deployment of technologies that remove greenhouse gases from the atmosphere to help bring temperatures back down.
Some delegations opposed including carbon-removal technologies, arguing that doing so could open the door to continued fossil fuel use.

“The fact there is loads of unfinished business at this COP shows there’s a big problem here,” said Brenda Mwale, Malawi’s loss and damage negotiator. “The question is, are we in a leadership crisis? Was there really a vision for this COP?” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Virginia child dies in state’s first measles-associated death of 2026
articles.summary:
Death adds to national measles outbreak that recently cost the US its measles elimination status after 26 years

Virginia reported…

blocks.text: Virginia reported its first measles-associated death of 2026 ⁠on Friday, involving a child who tested positive for the infectious disease, the state’s health department said.
The department said the child was ⁠age four or younger. It did not disclose additional details, including the child’s vaccination status, citing the family’s privacy.
The death adds to a worsening national measles outbreak that recently cost the US its measles elimination status after 26 years.
Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit US state, reported an eighth measles-related death and confirmed 1,631 measles cases as of Friday.
Wisconsin has ⁠also reported two deaths, while New York state recorded its first measles-associated ​death, involving a ​child.
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has confirmed six ​measles-associated deaths so far in 2026, though it does not ​specify the states ‌where the deaths were ​recorded.

A discrepancy between ​state and federal death tallies arose after the CDC, under the Trump administration’s health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, began using National Center for Health Statistics mortality data instead of state figures.
Virginia has reported 220 measles ⁠cases so far in 2026, including 40 among children four years old or younger and 75 among those age five to 12, state ⁠health department data showed as of Thursday.
Of those cases, 179 involved unvaccinated individuals, 39 were associated with people ‌whose vaccination status was ‌unknown and two occurred with vaccinated individuals.

“Virginia has not had a measles-related death ‌since 1978,” said Frederic Bertley, immunologist and chief executive officer of the Center of Science and Industry. Bertley added that the measles virus infection is both alarming and evidence that measles is gaining a foothold and becoming a growing problem for the US.

Virginia health officials have reported increased measles activity driven largely by outbreaks ‌in the state’s central region. Buckingham county has reported 127 cases, the most in the state, while neighboring Charlotte county has recorded 34 ​cases.

articles.title: PH, UK seek closer cooperation on nature protection, climate efforts
articles.summary: The Philippines and the United Kingdom are exploring expanded cooperation on nature financing, climate resilience and other environmental initiatives, the Department of Environment and Natural…

blocks.text: Published November 21, 2026 11:28pm

The Philippines and the United Kingdom are looking at ways to work more closely on protecting the environment, addressing climate change and funding nature conservation projects, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) said.
UK Special Representative for Nature Ruth Davis met with Environment Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna and other DENR officials during bilateral talks to discuss potential areas of collaboration.
Davis said both countries needed to move beyond pilot projects and secure financing to scale up mangrove protection, restoration and other nature-based solutions.

“The challenge for all of us is how we move beyond individual pilots and unlock the kind of financing needed to scale up mangrove protection, restoration, and other nature-based solutions,” Davis said, according to a DENR statement.
She also expressed interest in having British marine science organizations work with their Philippine counterparts.
Cuna said the Philippines faced various environmental threats, including rising temperatures and warmer seas that could harm coral reefs and fisheries.
He welcomed the proposed partnerships, noting ongoing domestic efforts to establish marine research stations and strengthen local scientific capabilities.
“Our priority is to ensure that environmental protection delivers tangible benefits for communities while supporting resilient and sustainable development,” Cuna said.
He added that the Philippines valued its partnership with the UK on climate, biodiversity and ocean issues.
The DENR said the Philippines was also advancing the National Blue Carbon Action Partnership, which is supported by the UK's Blue Planet Fund.
The initiative includes blue carbon mapping, carbon-stock assessments and the development of a Blue Carbon Public Finance Roadmap to guide sustainable investments.— MCG, GMA News
Follow GMA News Online on Facebook for real-time news and developments in the Philippines and around the world.

articles.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
articles.summary: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.

image.caption: Palm oil exports are part of the deal but will be closely regulatedImage: Willy Kurniawan/REUTERS

blocks.text: The European Union and Indonesia signed a free trade deal on Saturday, describing it as a new chapter in economic relations between the two sides.
"This is one of the most ambitious deals the European Union has concluded in Asia," Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, said at the signing ceremony on Saturday.
"Together, we represent a market of 730 million people," she added.

The Indonesia-European Union Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) and the additional Investment Protection Agreement (IPA) are designed to reduce trade barriers and attract investment in strategic sectors such as electric vehicles, electronics, and pharmaceuticals.
The agreement comes after almost 10 years of negotiations and is part of a wider series of trade deals by the EU.
'Keeping the doors open when others are closing theirs'
The bloc hopes to reduce its reliance on individual economic partners as trade with both China and the US has become more difficult in recent years.
Von der Leyen also stressed the importance of international cooperation, saying that "in a time when others are closing their doors, we keep ours open."

blocks.caption: In 2025, von der Leyen met with Indonesian President Pabowo Subianto to work on the agreementImage: Laily Rachev - Biro Pers Sekretariat Presiden

blocks.text: The deal sees tariffs on about 98% of EU exports to Indonesia to be done away with. The EU estimates that European companies could save more than €600 million (around €658 million) per year.

"The benefits for our exporters are concrete and measurable," Indonesian Minister of Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto said, hailing a "new chapter" in economic relations with the EU. He said the deal would benefit his country’s main exports to Europe, including palm oil, footwear and textiles.

Palm oil and deforestation had been major stumbling blocks during the negotiations, and the agreement includes mechanisms for cooperation on regulatory and sustainability issues as well as a dedicated protocol on palm oil to address environmental concerns.
The EU parliament is now expected to greenlight the deal while Indonesian authorities will also complete the ratification process so it can enter into force in 2027.

articles.title: New EU budget proposal aims at tax gobal tech giants
articles.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected…

image.caption: Costa says he is "confident that this proposal is a good basis for moving towards a final agreement" Image: Christopher Katsarov/ZUMA/IMAGO

blocks.text: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a new draft for the next EU budget.
Among other things, he is suggesting a tax on big tech firms to ease the contributions of member states, some of which strongly criticised earlier proposals.
The EU budget is theEuropean Union’s shared budget and it is used for things ranging from agricultural subsidies, infrastructure projects to border control and defence.

A first draft for the 2028 to 2034 budget was proposed by the EU Commission in 2025 but was criticised, especially by a group of northern European members including Germany who wanted the budget to be much smaller.
Following that criticism, the European Council President has now suggested a new draft, which is smaller by €204 billion.
But divisions among member states appear to remain, with France immediately coming out against Costa’s new draft, saying it was "deeply disappointing."

blocks.caption: The EU budget also covers financial aid for UkraineImage: Hans Lucas/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: What’s the plan for the tech tax?

The proposal includes a string of new "revenue channels," explicitly intended to "to keep national contributions at a reasonable level," so that member state will have to contribute less than otherwise would be the case.
The biggest splash would likely come from a tax on companies with an annual turnover from digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU and 750 million euros worldwide.

Those firms would be subject to "an annual contribution corresponding to 3% of the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data," according to Costa.
Aside from the tech tax, the "balanced basket of new own resources" also includes taxes on tobacco products and electronic waste.
What happens next?

Neither the EU Commission nor European Council President Costa will have the final word on the budget. Costa's plan will now be at the centre of hours of talks when EU leaders meet in Brussels next week.

"This is a realistic budget that addresses our new priorities while preserving our established policies," Costa wrote about his proposal. "I am confident that this proposal is a good basis for moving towards a final agreement."
But an initial reaction from France suggests that any final agreement might still be some way off.
The French presidency said the budget "falls well short ​of ‌what is needed, particularly on ‌the Common Agricultural Policy, ‌notably ​to guarantee income support for farmers."
"As it ⁠stands, ​this proposal ​from the President ​of the European ‌Council does not ​provide ⁠a basis for an ⁠agreement."
The EU was hoping to reach a general agreement on the budget by the end of 2026 with its formal adoption planned for 2027.

articles.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
articles.summary: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

image.caption: Kryvyi Rih is Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometownImage: Press service of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Russian ballistic missile strikes on Ukraine's southern city of Kryvyi Rih — President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown — killed two people and wounded dozens of others, local officials said Saturday.

The attacks come amid little progress in talks to end the nearly five-year-old war and after Ukraine, on three occasions this week, struck the Kerch bridge linking Russian-occupied Crimea with Russia.
Russian President Vladimir Putin had vowed a "painful" response to the Kerch attack, as the bridge is vital for war supplies for Russian forces in the south.
Russia intensifies aerial attacks on Ukraine
What do we know?
Among the dead in Friday evening's double-tap strikes on Kryvyi Rih were a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, while several children were among the 60 wounded, the Ukrainian officials said.

Several fires broke out and damage was caused to about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial facility, Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration, wrote on Telegram.
Moscow, meanwhile, confirmed a further strike on Friday night in Kryvyi Rih.
Russia's Defense Ministry said a thermal power plant in the city was hit, along with a power substation in the region of Rivne, on the opposite side of the country.
Both facilities supply electricity to the industry supporting Ukraine's military, the ministry added.

blocks.caption: Kryvyi Rih has been hit several times by Russia during the warImage: Press service of the National Police of Ukraine/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: What are the other latest developments?
Elsewhere in the nearly five-year-long war, Russia ​also struck a ​cargo vessel ‌near Odesa, which Moscow said was carrying dual-use goods ​for ⁠the Ukrainian military.
Eleven people, including two children, were wounded when a Russian drone attacked a five-story apartment building in the northeastern Kharkiv region, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Saturday.
One person was wounded in a Russian attack on the capital, Kyiv, according to the service.
In Russia, local officials said Saturday that Ukrainian drone attacks wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions.

Finland, meanwhile, said it detected a drone attack on Saturday morning on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea, prompting Prime Minister Petteri Orpo to warn that the war is "spilling over into our immediate vicinity."
After damage to Russia's Kerch bridge to Crimea, Zelenskyy warned in an interview with US broadcaster NBC that the structure "will not remain standing anyway."

articles.title: Princess of Wales speaks about impact of cancer diagnosis in BBC film Heal
articles.summary:
Documentary records Catherine taking on Three Peaks challenge and finding ‘sense of hope alongside uncertainty’

The Princess of Wales has spoken candidly about the impact of her cancer…

blocks.text: The Princess of Wales has spoken candidly about the impact of her cancer diagnosis in a BBC documentary to be aired later this month.

“Cancer does change you,” Catherine, 44, says in the trailer for the 30-minute programme. “It changes your body. It changes you physically, but there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.”

The film records Catherine taking on the Three Peaks challenge – climbing the three highest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales in 24 hours – and meeting with other people undergoing cancer treatment. Described by the BBC as a “highly personal film”, the documentary, titled Heal, will be shown on BBC One on 29 November.

blocks.caption: The Princess of Wales climbing Yr Wydffa in Snowdonia. Photograph: BBC/Kensington Palace/Matt Porteous

blocks.text: The trailer emerged as it was reported that King Charles will voluntarily pay “mansion tax” on relevant royal household properties, despite Crown exemption. The high-value council tax surcharge – often referred to as a mansion tax – will take effect in 2028 and apply to properties valued at more than £2m.
Catherine was diagnosed with an undisclosed form of cancer in early 2024, for which she received chemotherapy, and by January 2025 announced she was in remission.

She was treated at the Royal Marsden hospital in London, a world-leading oncology centre, with funds from the distribution of the documentary, which will also be broadcast in other countries, going to the Royal Marsden cancer charity.

When people successfully finish cancer treatment at the hospital they often ring a bell in celebration. “I didn’t ring the bell,” Catherine says in the trailer, speaking to her brothe, James Middleton as they are walking together.
“Maybe this is your ringing the bell,” he says, in reference to her undertaking the Three Peaks challenge and making the programme.

When she completed the challenge in June, 18 months after announcing that the cancer was in remission, she became the first royal to have achieved the feat – climbing Ben Nevis, Scafell Pike and Yr Wyddfa in less than 24 hours, having started on a Saturday evening.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Funds from the distribution of the film will go to the Royal Marsden cancer charity where Catherine was treated. Photograph: BBC/Kensington Palace/Matt Porteous

blocks.text: In the programme, which will be introduced by the presenter Kirsty Young, Catherine talks about how she has learned through her recovery to find “a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty”.
Kate Phillips, the BBC’s chief content officer, said she hoped the documentary “will resonate with BBC viewers and provide comfort and support to those navigating their own health challenges”.

articles.title: British man recalls ‘despair’ over son’s death after fall from Cyprus window
articles.summary:
Joshua Foster tells of moment he ‘lost control’ of two-year-old when he fell from fourth storey of hotel

A British father who was fined by the courts after his two-year-old son fell from a…

blocks.text: A British father who was fined by the courts after his two-year-old son fell from a fourth-floor window during a family holiday in Cyprus has recalled his “despair” when the boy slipped from his grasp.

Joshua Foster was handed a €3,000 (£2,500) penalty after he pleaded guilty to a charge of causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act. Prosecutors in Cyprus had refused to drop the case against him.

During recent court proceedings, it was heard that Foster thought the window at the King Evelthon Beach Hotel & Resort in Chlorakas was closed when he approached it with his son, Jaxon, to show him the view of a waterpark.
The 37-year-old “lost control” of him, the Paphos district court was told, before the boy plunged 10 metres (33ft). The fall happened on 12 July, the first day of the Fosters’ family holiday.

In an interview with the Daily Mail, Foster said: “I have a burden. I’ll have that my whole life. It’s very traumatic. My mind doesn’t want to go there. I just remember the despair of him falling, and watching him fall.
“It was just such a shock … I put him up thinking he was going against a glass pane … and then he wasn’t there.”
The toddler was pronounced dead at Paphos general hospital shortly after he suffered severe cranial injuries when he hit a veranda below.

Foster recalled his outpouring of emotion when he located his son after the fall. “I picked him up. I held him and screamed,” he said. The Essex-born auditor said he and his wife had an hour with their son’s body after he was pronounced dead.

The decision to charge Foster, reported to be a senior accountant at KPMG, was criticised by his legal representatives, as well as human rights defenders, media pundits and diplomats, arguing that it lacked compassion.

The charge Foster accepted is usually levelled in cases involving fatal traffic accidents. It carries a maximum penalty of four years in prison, but the fine he was handed was the lightest sentence possible for the offence.
At his sentencing in October, Judge Froso Christodoulidou ruled that Foster would not be jailed, before describing the incident as a “tragic event”.
The court had heard that, while the presence of alcohol had been detected in Foster’s blood, it was not enough to suggest he was impaired to the point where he had “acted recklessly”.
Foster was detained after the fall. He reportedly had to tell his eldest child, a daughter, about her brother’s death via a video call while he was being held.

He posted €30,000 (£26,000) in bail to return to the UK to attend the funeral of his son in August, but was forced, under threat of extradition, to return to Cyprus and surrender his passport by 14 September.

In a push for clemency, Foster’s legal team had appealed in September to the island’s attorney general, Cyprus’s top legal official, to discontinue the criminal procedure on humanitarian grounds. The request was denied.
Since returning home, Foster said the focus of his grieving family had turned to their daughter.
“It’s very difficult,” he said. “She waves at the sky and says: ‘I love you’ to him and blows a kiss. She’s lost her best friend. She’s gone from having a sibling to being an only child.”

articles.title: Russian strike on Zelenskyy's hometown in central Ukraine kills 2, wounds 60
articles.summary: A Russian strike on the centre of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown, Kryvyi Rih, killed two people and wounded 60 others, local officials said Saturday.

image.caption: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at a news briefing in Copenhagen, Denmark, on Nov. 10. (Emil Helms/Ritzau Scanpix/Reuters)

blocks.text: A Russian strike on the centre of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown, Kryvyi Rih, killed two people and wounded 60 others, local officials said Saturday.

A seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman were killed in the attack Friday night on the city in central Ukraine, the head of the city administration, Oleksandr Vilkul, wrote on the Telegram messaging service.
Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, said 60 people were wounded, including six children.
The strike caused four fires and damaged about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial facility, as well as businesses and vehicles, Vilkul said.
The attack fits the pattern of Moscow's heavy responses to eye-catching Ukrainian attacks, such as the ones this week on the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to illegally annexed Crimea.
The site of a Russian drone and missile attack on Friday night in central Kryvyi Rih, Zelenskyy's hometown. (Press service of the National Police of Ukraine/Reuters)

The missile attack came hours after two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland, in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine.
European troops were taking part on Friday in an unprecedented two-week military exercise that began Nov. 9 in southeastern Poland.

items: Trump greets 'my friend' Putin at China summit

blocks.text: Forces are preparing for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine aimed at helping to stabilize the country and rebuild its military.
European countries previously have expressed alarm at what they deem to be Russia's attempts to destabilize the continent.
The aftermath of Friday night's Russian drone and missile attack in central Kryvyi Rih. The attack killed two people, including a child. (Press service of the National Police of Ukraine/Reuters)
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said in Warsaw on Saturday that the alliance is commited to defending "every inch of ​Polish territory."
The development stoked tensions between Europe and Moscow as the U.S. tried to build momentum for talks on ending the war, which began with Russia's invasion on Feb. 24, 2022.

U.S. President Donald Trump discussed the war with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at a summit in China on Thursday, according to his envoy, Steve Witkoff. Trump called Putin his "friend" during the meeting and continued to tout their relationship at a White House news conference on Friday.

David McGuinty, Canada's defence minister, said in an interview with CBC's Adrienne Arsenault that Ottawa and leaders in Europe are anticipating the Trump administration will become "less forthcoming" in its support for Ukraine, but noted Canada is staying the course.
"The United States is going to do what the United States is going to do as a sovereign country," McGuinty said.
"But we're … working hand-in-glove with our European colleagues to make sure that the Ukrainians get the support they need."
Zelenskyy calls Putin 'a killer'
Asked about Trump's remarks in an interview with CNN, Zelenskyy called Putin "a killer."
"For us, he is an enemy. And of course, for us, he is a killer," Zelenskyy said Friday. He warned that describing the Russian leader in friendly terms could mean "he doesn't feel enough pressure."
Trump, Xi and Putin release 'peace declaration' with no mention of Ukraine or Iran

Elsewhere in Ukraine, 11 people, including two children, were wounded when a Russian drone attacked a five-storey apartment building in the Kharkiv region, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Saturday. One person was wounded in a Russian attack on the capital, Kyiv, according to the service.
In Russia, local officials said Saturday that Ukrainian drone attacks wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions.
A firefighter works at the site of a Russian missile strike in Kyiv, during Russia's attack on Ukraine on Friday night into Saturday. (Press service of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine/Reuters)
Russian cargo vessel on fire in Finnish waters
Meanwhile, Russian officials said on Saturday that a cargo vessel bound for Kaliningrad was attacked by two drones in neutral waters.
The crew was being evacuated and the extent of the damage was being assessed, said Aleksandr Drozdenko, the Leningrad regional governor, shortly after the attack was first reported.

The ship caught fire after being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea and later drifted into Finnish waters, prompting Helsinki to impose temporary air and maritime restrictions. It said Ukraine was probably behind the attack.
The Russian cargo ship Sparta II is seen damaged in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday. (Finnish Border Guard/Reuters)
Finland's Border Guard said there was no danger to people or maritime traffic, that rescue units were at the scene, and that it was co-ordinating operations with neighbouring countries.
The Sparta II vessel is known to have links to Russia's armed forces, Finnish Border Guard Cmdr. Ilja Iljin told Reuters.
"At the moment, there is no confirmed information about what cargo is on board, but it cannot be ruled out that there is military material on board," he said.

items: Russia fires hundreds of missiles, drones at Ukraine — and allegedly into Poland

blocks.text: "The war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas. Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said on X.
Ukraine's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Russia's embassy in Helsinki did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The vessel is subject to U.S. sanctions and is linked to Russian shipping company Oboronlogistika, according to the U.S. Treasury Department.
Oboronlogistika provides logistics services for the Russian defence ministry, according to the company's website.

Kaliningrad Gov. Alexei Besprozvannykh said the incident posed no threat to supplies to the region. Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave on the Baltic Sea that borders Poland and Lithuania, has occasionally been a flashpoint between Russia, the European Union and NATO.

articles.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
articles.summary: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.

blocks.text: A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities.
Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores was detained along with his lieutenant by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said.

Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI. The US is seeking his extradition.
Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump since he returned to the White House.

Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, is thought to have been active in the drug trafficking trade since the 1990s but managed to evade authorities till now by maintaining a relatively low profile.

Using US intelligence on his whereabouts, Mexican special forces descended on his location using "stealth and surprise", establishing a perimeter to prevent him from escaping and reinforcements arriving, Mexico's defence secretariat said.
However, they "came under attack from gunfire and explosives" before entering the property and arresting Meza Flores and his second-in-command, it added.
Videos circulating online appear to show helicopters firing streams of bullets towards the ground in Guasave. Others appear to show people at a baseball stadium fleeing as they hear shooting sounds.
The two detainees were subsequently flown to Mexico City to face prosecution, the defence secretariat said.
When he was added to the FBI's most-wanted list in 2025, he was accused of "heinous crimes" including kidnapping, extortion and torture.
Then-acting FBI director Brian Driscoll said Meza Flores and his organisation had also unleashed a "scourge of illicit drugs" into the US via its southern border with Mexico.
He was initially charged with drug trafficking in the US in 2012 before being charged again in 2019.
The 44-year-old is alleged to have conspired to manufacture and distribute large quantities of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana between 2005 and 2019.
Meza Flores was originally a high-ranking member of the Beltrán Leyva Organization, but a split between rival factions led to a surge of violence and prompted him to establish his own cartel by 2013.

His organisation has also engaged in what US officials described as an "extremely violent turf war" with the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most powerful drug trafficking gangs, which operates in the same region.
Meza Flores was added to the FBI's most-wanted list after Mexican authorities reportedly linked his cartel to 20 million fentanyl pills they seized in 2024.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has taken a tougher stance on the country's cartels in a bid to resist US intervention on Mexican soil. Mexico has welcomed closer collaboration but resisted US boots on the ground.
Trump made stemming the flow of drugs into the US across its southern border one of his key election pledges.

articles.title: A real '3 Body Problem': Astronomers discover a nearby 'weirdo' triple-star system
articles.summary: An international team of astronomers led by the University of Montreal has found a nearby triple-star system, much like the one in the Netflix show 3 Body Problem. But this one seems to be… a little…

image.caption: An artistic illustration shows the Welopō'ai triple-star system, located just 28 light-years from Earth. The system consists of a red dwarf star, right, and a closely orbiting white dwarf, left, with a second white dwarf, upper, orbiting the pair at a much greater distance. (Benoît Gougeon/Universit

blocks.text: Roughly 28 light-years from Earth lies a peculiar star system called IRAS 21500+5903.

For years, astronomers had known about the two stars that orbited one another. But then, when looking for exoplanets — planets that orbit other stars — a group of astronomers made a surprising discovery: there was another star in the system. Instead of being a binary star system, this was a triple-star system.

"It's a freak thing. It was an annoying object," said Étienne Artigau, a researcher at the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets (IREx) at the University of Montreal. "It's not what we were looking for."
Their findings were released this week in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

The system contains a red dwarf, a type of star that is very common in our galaxy, and two smaller, dense white dwarfs. One is roughly 1,000 astronomical units (the distance between the sun and Earth) away from the red dwarf. The other, they found, was a mere two astronomical units away, a little similar to the distance from the sun to Mars.
The inner white dwarf orbits the red dwarf, while the outer white dwarf orbits the pair.
A quirky neighbour
What's surprising is that no one had discovered it over the decades.

"It's weird that no one found the system, but it also says that there are weird things overlooked just next to us," Artigau said. "It's like not next door, but down the road, just one block away of a stellar neighbourhood."

When a low- to medium-mass star reaches the end of its life, it first swells into a red giant before leaving behind the dense and small white dwarf. It is what will happen to our own sun in roughly five billion years.
This artist concept depicts an ultra-dense dead star, called a white dwarf, passing in front of a small red star. (NASA/JPL-Caltech)

While looking for an exoplanet in this system, the international team of astronomers — led by the University of Montreal team — used an instrument at the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope in Maunakea, Hawaii, called SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou). It is used to detect exoplanets and does this by measuring tiny changes in a star's velocity, which can be caused by orbiting planets.
But the red dwarf wasn't doing what it was supposed to be doing. It was moving differently, with velocity changes of nearly 16 kilometres a second. That's a huge difference.
Initially, they thought it was a brown dwarf, a type of substellar object that has a mass of about 75 times that of Jupiter.
But that still didn't make sense.
More weirdness
The velocities were so off that they broke Artigau's code.

"At some point, we said, Okay, we should get to the end of it. Something's wrong with that object. And so I fixed the code," he said. "And then we just said, let me do the math of that brown dwarf. Okay, no, it doesn't work."
It was a real head-scratcher.

items: Are we alone? Institute searching for alien signals is using a new way to answer that age-old question
Astronomers think they've captured a planet forming around a host star — something never seen before

blocks.text: What they eventually discovered is that what was causing the perturbations was a high-mass… something. But it also couldn't be seen.
Could it be a black hole? A neutron star? A white dwarf?

The team turned to the Gemini North telescope, also on Maunakea. Using high-resolution images from its 'Alopeke instrument — a specialized high-speed camera — they found what they were looking for: a faint companion star — a white dwarf — orbiting closely around the red dwarf.
Here's where it gets weirder.

Before becoming a white dwarf, the star would have become a red giant. As it swelled up, its orbit would have been so close to the red dwarf that the pair must have interacted with one another. Many times these types of stars envelop the red dwarf, or the two may even merge. This didn't happen.
And there was more.
The inner white dwarf should be spiralling inward toward the red dwarf. Instead, it is in a stable orbit.
It could be that the more distant white dwarf is somehow stabilizing the orbit, though they don't know yet how. That's for future research.

The image on the left shows the two components of the system: Welopō'ai A, a closely orbiting red dwarf and white dwarf pair, and Welopō'ai B, a second white dwarf located farther away. The image on the right provides a close-up view of the inner pair and their orbital paths. (Pan-STARRS1/STScI/MAST, left, International Gemini Observatory/NSF NOIRLab, right. Graphical construction by Étienne Artigau & Heidi White (UdeM/IREx))
"We're saying it cannot exist," Artigau said. "Of course, it exists. It's there."
Paul Delaney, professor emeritus of physics and astronomy at York University in Toronto, believes that perhaps the more distant white dwarf was once much closer to the other pair.

"I mean, when planetary systems form now, one of the standard things is migration," he said. "I would bet that they were relatively proximate to each other and then they did engage in a bit of gravitational embracing, and the further white dwarf today was much, much closer in its heyday."

To add to the weirdness, the astronomers calculated that the system is roughly 10 billion years old, older than our own solar system of 4.6 billion years, and its stars are metal-rich. Typically, these older stars are metal-poor.
"It's tantalizing, and we just don't know if it means anything. It may just be a random draw basically of a stellar population," Artigau said.
Still searching for an exoplanet

The astronomers gave this system the Hawaiian name Welopō'ai, combining "welo" which means an inherited family trait, and "pō'ai," which means an orbit or circular path. The name therefore means "path of family traits."
The very popular book and Netflix show 3 Body Problem looks at a triple-star system and the effects it could have on a nearby planet, mainly to a civilization that has evolved on that planet.
One of the terms that is used to describe the triple-star system in the show is "chaotic," which affects the speed at which the civilization can evolve.

The issue is an age-old physics problem. Two-body systems are predictable. But add a third, and everything blows up. That's because Body A pulls on Body B and Body C. Body C in turn pulls on Body A and Body B, and because of these interactions, it changes their motions and their forces forever.
While researchers didn't find an exoplanet, Artigau said the search isn't over.
"It's such a weirdo system that Atanas Stefanov, one of the authors, he's applying for time to get, to look for planets around the red dwarf," he said.
Whether there is a planet there or whether an alien civilization could live on a planet in a triple-star system remains to be seen.
For Artigau, he said the fact that something new was thrown at him was very exciting.
"I like it," he said. "Little things that are just sideways in your life in research. It's fun."
